Use the official solutions as the first approach. `source.contest` is e.g. "Gauss Contest (CEMC)", "Pascal Contest (CEMC)", "Euclid Contest (CEMC)". See `data/raw/cemc/gauss7-2016.json` for the finished format. Other agents work on other CEMC slugs at the same time; touch only your own. Full-solution contests with parts: one question per part (ids like `cemc-fryer-2012-02c`); short-answer parts with a single value numeric/text, explanations/proofs and parts asking for several values `self`. Match the conventions of existing `data/raw/cemc/fryer-*.json` files (else `euclid-2018.json`). Grades "9" Fryer, "10" Galois, "11" Hypatia. If the three papers of a year share a problem, extract it in the lowest grade and mark the others `duplicateOf`. Slugs `fryer-<Y>`, `galois-<Y>`, `hypatia-<Y>`. Points as printed (split a problem's 10 marks sensibly if parts are unmarked).
